overview: Red Mountain Mining District is a high-altitude industrial landscape centered on Red Mountain Pass and spanning portions of Ouray and San Juan Counties.
Mining intensified in the late 1870s and 1880s around rich breccia-pipe, chimney, and vein deposits carrying silver, gold, lead, zinc, and copper.

G3 closed 2026-08-21: use an interpretive parent-district envelope centered on Red Mountain Pass and the US 550 / Red Mountain Creek–Mineral Creek corridor, from northern Ironton Park south through the Red Mountains toward Chattanooga/Mineral Creek and Mount Abram, and west to the divide above Red Mountain Creek.
Timeline: intensive exploration/mining developed in the late 1870s–1880s; Red Mountain was one of the original Ouray County mining districts recognized in 1882.

moreHistory: The boom supported Red Mountain Town/Rogersville, Guston, Ironton, Chattanooga/Sweetville, and other camps.
A wagon road connected the district by 1885, and the Silverton Railroad traversed it by 1889.
Surviving features include headframes, mine and mill ruins, cabins and boardinghouses, dumps, rail grades, road traces, flumes, and townsites.
Treat the district as parent context and preserve named towns, mines, roads, and railroad features as separate linked records.
Do not provide directions into workings, unstable structures, or restricted parcels.
